***
#
Datapedia
: Automated proctoring ***
🏠👀Have you ever sat an exam at home with a programme watching you for signs of cheating?
That’s automated proctoring.
🤖AI-powered software analyses webcam, microphone and screen activity to check your identity (often through facial scans) and flags behaviour it considers suspicious. Its use has skyrocketed since the pandemic, from universities to professional certification exams.
The data protection concern 🔒🫆 is that these tools can be highly intrusive, because they capture video 📹 and audio 🔊 from private spaces. What’s more, their AI can wrongly flag some students as cheating, particularly those from minority groups or with conditions such as autism or dyslexia.
And if your university requires it, can you really say no?
That power imbalance has implications for what ‘consent’ means.

EDPS Press Release
✈️ EU-US border information exchange: effective safeguards are essential to protect fundamental rights in practice.
A new EDPS Opinion comments on the European Commission’s proposal for a framework agreement between the EU and the US on sharing information to verify, screen and vet travellers. The proposed framework would set common conditions for the reciprocal exchange of data between the authorities of EU Member States and the US for border checks, travel authorisations and visas. The proposal is linked to a US requirement for partner countries in the US Visa Waiver Program to conclude an ‘Enhanced Border Security Partnership’ by the end of 2026.
The Opinion sets out the safeguards needed to keep the processing of personal data limited to what is strictly necessary and proportionate. Its recommendations include:
• the possible offences considered as presenting risks to ‘public order’ and ‘public security’ should be clearly specified;
• competent authorities should establish an objective link between the risk and the individual concerned on a case-by-case basis;
• the Commission should monitor whether judicial redress is available in practice for anyone affected, regardless of their citizenship or nationality.
@
Supervisor
Wojciech Wiewiórowski said: “This would be the first time the EU agrees to share personal data, including biometrics, with a third country on this scale for border control. All the necessary safeguards must be in place to ensure the protection of individuals, including real oversight on both sides of the Atlantic.”

*** Spain Digital Week ***
Digital humanism as the compass for the AI era.
At Spain Digital Week, organised by Adigital at the Permanent Representation of Spain to the EU, the EDPS
@
Secretary_General
Leonardo Cervera-Navas delivered a speech on the role of the EDPS in a world increasingly governed by AI.
He described AI as an amplifier, of both the benefits of digitalisation and its risks, particularly where automated decisions affect people who do not know a machine is involved.
“AI amplifies the good brought forth by digitalization allowing for greater efficiency, improved access to services and new opportunities. But it also exacerbates the bad, raising considerable risks as automated decisions are susceptible of profoundly affecting the lives of individuals.” Leonardo Cervera-Navas noted.
He explained how the EDPS’s role has evolved: in addition to supervising EU institutions under the EUDPR, the EDPS is now a notified body and market surveillance authority under the AI Act. He presented two initiatives to strengthen coordination across the EU digital rulebook: the AI Act Correspondents Network and the proposed Digital Clearinghouse 2.0.
The Secretary General also stressed that reducing administrative burden and protecting fundamental rights are two different exercises, as the European Data Protection Board and EDPS warned in their joint opinion on the omnibus proposal.
“In a world where AI is becoming embedded in how we live and work, trust may become one of the most valuable qualities the EU digital infrastructure will have to offer. At the EDPS, we are working hard to build and protect that trust because we strongly believe that it is the key for a sustainable digital future.” Leonardo Cervera-Navas added.

candidates.title: STATEMENT OF THE NATIONAL PRIVACY COMMISSION ON REPORTED DATA LEAKS INVOLVING GOVERNMENT AGENCIES
candidates.feed_text: QUEZON CITY, 06 November 2026 - The National Privacy Commission (NPC) is aware of reports concerning alleged data leaks involving several government agencies on 5 November 2026. According to NPC Spokesperson and Deputy Privacy Commissioner Atty. Jose Belarmino II, as of 6 November 2026, the Commission has not received personal data breach notifications from the concerned government agencies in relation to the reported incidents. The Commission will coordinate directly with the government agencies identified in these reports to verify the alleged incidents, ascertain the circumstances surrounding them, and determine whether personal data have been compromised. Where warranted, the Commission will require the concerned agencies to submit the necessary reports and comply with their obligations under the Data Privacy Act of 2012 and applicable NPC issuances. Under NPC Circular No. 16-03, personal information controllers (PICs) are required to notify the Commission and affected data subjects within 72 hours upon knowledge of, or reasonable belief that, a personal data breach requiring mandatory notification has occurred. Should the reported incidents be confirmed and meet the requirements for mandatory notification, the concerned agencies must submit the prescribed personal data breach notifications in accordance with existing regulations. The Commission emphasizes that reports of alleged data leaks do not, by themselves, establish that a personal data breach has occurred or that the provisions of the Data Privacy Act of 2012 have been violated. Such determinations require an assessment of the facts and circumstances surrounding each incident. The NPC will continue to monitor developments and take appropriate regulatory action, as warranted, to ensure the protection of personal data and uphold the rights of data subjects. Further information will be provided as appropriate, subject to developments in the matter. ### The post STATEMENT OF THE NATIONAL PRIVACY COMMISSION ON REPORTED DATA LEAKS INVOLVING GOVERNMENT AGENCIES appeared first on National Privacy Commission .

candidates.title: NPC, Globe Collaborate to Strengthen Privacy Awareness and Online Safety for Filipino Youth
candidates.feed_text: QUEZON CITY — The National Privacy Commission (NPC) and Globe Telecom, Inc. (Globe) formalized their collaboration through a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) on 19 October 2026 at The Upper Class Tower in Quezon City to promote privacy awareness, digital wellness, responsible technology use, and online safety, particularly among Filipino youth. The NPC was represented by Privacy Commissioner Atty. Johann Carlos S. Barcena, CESO III, while Globe was represented by Chief Privacy Officer and Head of the Digital Policy and Governance Group, Atty. Irish Krystle Salandanan-Almeida. The collaboration establishes a framework for joint educational initiatives, public awareness campaigns, and capacity-building activities aimed at helping Filipinos better understand data protection and navigate the digital environment responsibly. “It takes a village to raise a child. That village should extend to the digital world. Children should not have to choose between enjoying the benefits of technology and being safe online. They deserve both. And that requires digital literacy to go hand in hand with privacy awareness, responsible technology use, and the protection of their rights,” Privacy Commissioner Barcena said. Scope of collaboration Under the MOU, the NPC and Globe will explore initiatives that promote data protection, digital citizenship, digital wellness, and the responsible use of emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI). “Through this Memorandum of Understanding, the National Privacy Commission and Globe are establishing a framework for collaboration that can bring these lessons closer to children and the adults responsible for their welfare,” Privacy Commissioner Barcena added. The collaboration will support the NPC’s Kabataang Digital Program, which promotes digital citizenship, privacy awareness, and safe online behavior among young Filipinos. Through its Kabataang Digital Regional Caravan, the NPC conducts lectures on the fundamentals of the Data Privacy Act of 2012 (DPA), the safe and responsible use of gadgets and applications, and the rights of data subjects. Globe may participate in selected activities through speaking engagements and the sharing of learning materials. Globe will also share videos and other educational content from its Digital Thumbprint Program for use in the NPC’s awareness campaigns, events, training sessions, and public engagements. “Protecting people online goes beyond having strong privacy policies and safeguards. People also need the knowledge and confidence to understand their rights, recognize risks, and make informed decisions whenever they go online,” said Atty. Salandanan-Almeida. “By continuing our work with the National Privacy Commission, we can bring practical privacy and digital safety education closer to the people and communities who need it,” she added. The collaboration highlights the importance of cooperation between the government and the private sector in making privacy education more accessible and relevant to the public. ### The post NPC, Globe Collaborate to Strengthen Privacy Awareness and Online Safety for Filipino Youth appeared first on National Privacy Commission .

candidates.title: PUBLIC ADVISORY: NPC Calls on Digital Platforms to Ensure Compliance
candidates.feed_text: The National Privacy Commission (NPC) reminds all digital platform operators to strictly adhere to their heightened responsibilities and legal obligations in processing the personal data of child users in light of recent reports linking children's unrestricted access to social media, online gaming platforms, and digital content to exposure to violent activities and tragic offline incidents including school mass shootings. Social media applications, online platforms, digital services, and game developers accessible to minors in the Philippines are legally bound to comply with Republic Act No. 10173, otherwise known as the Data Privacy Act of 2012 (DPA); the Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of RA 10173; and related NPC circulars, advisory opinions, and issuances, particularly directives regarding Privacy by Design, automated processing, and the processing of children’s personal data and the personal data of vulnerable groups. To protect children from online violence and unmonitored digital exposure, social media companies, online platforms, and game developers are called upon to implement effective, privacy-preserving age-assurance mechanisms to restrict minors from accessing platforms or features intended for mature audiences and to cease behavioral profiling that pushes violent, aggressive, or unsafe content to child users. The NPC emphasizes that adherence to the fundamental principles of transparency, legitimate purpose, and proportionality is essential to responsible participation in the digital economy. Failure to ensure compliance with the Data Privacy Act of 2012, its IRR, and related NPC issuances may result in formal compliance orders, cease-and-desist orders, administrative sanctions, and criminal prosecution, as applicable, under Sections 25 to 33 of RA 10173. The NPC remains committed to protecting the rights of the data subject and ensuring a secure digital environment for vulnerable users, especially children. ### The post PUBLIC ADVISORY: NPC Calls on Digital Platforms to Ensure Compliance appeared first on National Privacy Commission .

candidates.feed_text: QUEZON CITY, PHILIPPINES — On September 22, 2026, the National Privacy Commission (NPC) issued Show Cause Orders to Meta, Roblox, Reddit, and Discord in relation to their non-compliance with applicable registration requirements under the Data Privacy Act of 2012 (DPA) and NPC Circular 2022-04. The issuance of the Show Cause Orders forms part of the NPC’s continuing exercise of its mandate to administer and enforce the DPA, its Implementing Rules and Regulations, and relevant issuances. As digital platforms become increasingly integrated into the everyday lives of Filipinos, including children and young people, the NPC recognizes the importance of ensuring that personal data processed through these platforms is handled lawfully, fairly, securely, and in a manner that respects the rights of data subjects. Intensified Compliance Investigation The NPC is intensifying its compliance monitoring and investigation of digital platforms whose services involve the processing of personal data of individuals in the Philippines. As part of this initiative, the NPC will assess compliance with applicable data protection laws, rules, and regulations, including requirements relating to registration, transparency, lawful processing, data subject rights, accountability, and appropriate organizational, physical, and technical security measures. These efforts constitute NPC’s continuing mandate to promote responsible data processing and safer digital spaces, particularly for children and young people. The NPC will take appropriate regulatory action against entities found to be non-compliant with data protection laws, rules, and regulations. Protecting the Privacy and Rights of Minor Data Subjects It is NPC’s position that the safety, privacy, and overall well-being of our youth must always come first. As learning and social interaction increasingly take place across both physical campuses and digital spaces, we are dedicated to protecting the privacy and data subject rights of our youth and promoting responsible data processing. The NPC calls on digital platforms, government agencies, parents, educational institutions, and other stakeholders to work together in promoting digital environments that respect privacy, protect personal data, and empower young people to exercise their rights. Protecting young people in the digital environment is a shared responsibility. Within its mandate, the NPC will continue to ensure that organizations processing personal data are held accountable and that the rights guaranteed to data subjects under Philippine data protection law are respected. ### The post STATEMENT OF THE NATIONAL PRIVACY COMMISSION ON INTENSIFIED OVERSIGHT OF DIGITAL PLATFORMS TO PROTECT CHILDREN’S PRIVACY appeared first on National Privacy Commission .

candidates.title: NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC: Use of Real Persons’ Likenesses in AI-Generated Images
candidates.feed_text: The National Privacy Commission (Commission) has observed the increasing circulation of synthetic media such as images and videos generated through artificial intelligence (AI) tools depicting real, identifiable persons. The Commission reminds the public that a person's face and likeness are personal information under Republic Act No. 10173, otherwise known as the Data Privacy Act of 2012 (DPA). 1 In fact, in certain instances, photographic and videographic media may also constitute biometric information that directly identifies an individual. 2 Using AI tools to generate an image or video from a real person's face and likeness and posting or sharing the resulting image and/or video, are forms of processing of personal data, whatever the nature or purpose of the resulting media. Like any processing of personal data, these acts must have a legitimate purpose and must conform with any of the criteria for lawful processing found under the DPA. While consent of the person depicted is the most recognizable criterion, the DPA provides other bases, which may be applicable depending on the circumstances of each case. Nevertheless, the use of a person’s face and likeness to create synthetic media without any lawful basis may amount to unauthorized processing under Section 25 of the DPA, and, depending on the extent of such processing, including the posting and sharing of such AI-generated media, may also constitute violations of the DPA’s other penal provisions. These violations carry criminal penalties and possible civil and administrative liabilities without prejudice to remedies found in other laws. 3 The Commission emphasizes that a fabricated image or video is false personal data. AI-generated media that depicts a real person doing something the person never did, saying something the person never said, or being somewhere the person never was, is false information about that person. Under Section 16(e) of the DPA, a data subject may demand the blocking, removal, or destruction of personal data upon substantial proof that the data is false, and this right may be enforced through a complaint before the Commission. While the Commission recognizes that satire, parody, commentary, and reporting on matters of public interest may fall under the constitutional right to freedom of speech, of expression, or of the press, and that the DPA does not apply to the processing of personal data for journalistic, artistic, or literary purposes, 4 these protections only attach to the purposes behind the use of a person’s likeness to the minimum extent suitable and necessary to achieve them. Whether the use of AI-generated media depicting a person’s face and likeness falls under any of these purposes depends on the circumstances of each instance, including whether the image is presented as real, whether its synthetic character is disclosed, and whether the use of the person’s actual photorealistic likeness is necessary such purpose. These reminders apply with equal force to AI-generated media of public officials. Public officials are data subjects under the DPA. While their right to privacy should be weighed against the right to information on matters of public concern, 5 a fabricated image or video depicts no actual conduct and conveys no information about the discharge of any official function. Family members of public officials who do not themselves hold public office, above all minor children, are private individuals entitled to the full protection of the DPA, and the Commission will treat complaints involving the likenesses of minors with utmost priority. A person whose likeness has been misused in an AI-generated media may demand its removal from the person or entity that posted or circulated it, and may file a complaint with the Commission. The Commission, in turn, may investigate the matter on the basis of the complaint or on its own initiative and may issue compliance and/or cease-and-desist orders during such investigation where warranted. 6 Copies of such orders may be furnished to online platforms and relevant government agencies for appropriate action. Online platforms are expected to provide accessible mechanisms for reporting such content and for promptly removing them based on lawful demands made by affected persons, in accordance with applicable law and their own policies. The Commission reminds all persons who create, post, and/or share AI-generated synthetic media to respect the rights and dignity of individuals, and to act promptly and in good faith to remove such content upon lawful demand of the affected persons. ### 1 Data Privacy Act of 2012, Republic Act No. 10173, Sec. 3(g). 2 See National Privacy Commission, Advisory Opinion No. 2023-025. 3 R.A. No. 10173 Sec. 12 (Criteria for Lawful Processing of Personal Information) and Sec. 25 (Unauthorized Processing of Personal Information and Sensitive Personal Information). 4 Implementing Rules and Regulations of R.A. No. 10173, Sections 5 and 5(b). 5 See NPC Advisory No. 2022-01 (Guidelines on Requests for Personal Data of Public Officers). 6 R.A. No. 10173, Sec. 7. candidates.title: NPC strengthens regional ties and advances data privacy standards at the 65th APPA Forum in Hong Kong, SAR China
candidates.feed_text: HONG KONG, SAR CHINA- The National Privacy Commission (NPC) of the Philippines executed a bilateral affirmation of cooperation, presented its regulatory framework on data scraping, and shared strategies for protecting children’s data at the 65th Asia Pacific Privacy Authorities (APPA) Forum. The forum was held from 16 to 17 June 2026, at Kowloon Shangri-La, Hong Kong, SAR China. Hosted by the Office of the Privacy Commissioner for Personal Data (PCPD), Hong Kong, SAR China, the two-day event gathered 16 member authorities and more than 100 delegates from around the world to address pressing regulatory concerns, with a particular focus on the legislative, enforcement, and security challenges emerging from Artificial Intelligence (AI) and other modern technologies. Strengthening cross-border cooperation The NPC and PCPD also signed the Affirmation of Cooperation in Personal Data Protection between the two authorities. Executed by Philippine Privacy Commissioner Atty. Johann Carlos S. Barcena and Hong Kong Privacy Commissioner for Personal Data Ada CHUNG Lai-ling, the affirmation revitalizes a framework initially established through a Memorandum of Understanding dated 22 May 2023. The affirmation recognizes the growing importance of cross-border cooperation in personal data protection and privacy governance, provides a framework for continued collaboration and information exchange on regulatory developments to secure the data privacy rights of individuals across both jurisdictions. “Cross-border threats require united global regulatory fronts, and our active engagement at the APPA Forum demonstrates the Philippine government's commitment to building a safe, transparent, and resilient digital ecosystem where innovation thrives alongside respect and adherence to data privacy rights,” said Privacy Commissioner Barcena. The NPC, as the Global Privacy Assembly (GPA) Secretariat, also engaged in a bilateral meeting with the Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada (OPC Canada) in its capacity as the GPA Chair. The discussions aimed at strengthening working cooperation between the NPC and the OPC Canada, while reviewing their parallel obligations as co-regulators on the global stage. Both regulatory bodies exchanged views on ongoing enforcement strategies, explored pathways to optimize and align regional legal frameworks with international data mandates, and shared their strategic institutional priorities moving forward. Advancing regulatory policy and youth advocacy During the forum's jurisdictional reporting session, the NPC, represented by Privacy Commissioner Barcena, presented its recent regulatory measures by discussing Advisory No. 2026-01, or the Guidelines on Data Scraping of Publicly Available Personal Data, which was issued on 13 April 2026. The presentation reinforced that information published online does not automatically constitute consent for unrestricted collection or processing. The guidelines mandate that organizations deploying web-scraping technologies must establish explicit, lawful purposes, carry out formal Privacy Impact Assessments, and implement appropriate safeguards when dealing with the personal data of vulnerable sectors, such as minors and persons with disabilities. “Accountability is a central theme: PICs remain responsible for compliance even when scraping is outsourced, must maintain documentation, and adopt retention and secure disposal policies. The Advisory also restricts harmful uses of scraped data, including doxxing, unauthorized profiling, surveillance, and discriminatory practices,” Privacy Commissioner Barcena highlighted. Furthering the country's active involvement, NPC Deputy Privacy Commissioner Atty. Juan Paolo Fajardo served as an expert panelist during a plenary session dedicated to protecting children's data and privacy in the age of social media platforms and AI. Highlighting that a child who understands her rights is far harder to exploit, he detailed the NPC’s multi-layered approach to child privacy. This includes the enforcement of NPC Advisory No. 2024-03, which establishes explicit guidelines on child-oriented transparency by requiring organizations to utilize clear, child-friendly notices, leverage accessible formats like video and animation, and mandate high-privacy default settings to secure youth processing systems against emerging AI-driven risks. Deputy Privacy Commissioner Fajardo also discussed the Kabataang Digital advocacy program of the NPC where the agency conducts school-to-school caravans to teach young students about data privacy and safe use of internet. “For us, this was never simply about compliance. It is about something plainer: that children can take part in digital life safely, confidently, and with dignity. Our experience suggests that education and design-driven regulation, working together, can deliver protection that lasts—even as AI reshapes the ground beneath us," Deputy Privacy Commissioner Fajardo emphasized. The NPC’s participation in the 65th APPA Forum underscores the Philippines’ continued commitment to international privacy cooperation and responsible digital governance. Through active diplomacy and unified regulatory frameworks, the NPC remains dedicated to establishing a resilient data protection ecosystem that leaves no Filipino behind. ### The post NPC strengthens regional ties and advances data privacy standards at the 65th APPA Forum in Hong Kong, SAR China appeared first on National Privacy Commission .

candidates.title: PAW 2026: NPC celebrates a decade of privacy leadership, calls for responsible AI governance
candidates.feed_text: The National Privacy Commission (NPC), with the support of the Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT), celebrated the National Data Privacy Awareness Week (PAW) with the theme “ANAMNESIS: Looking Back and Moving Forward”, highlighting a decade of advancing data privacy and protection in the Philippines. The culminating two-day event, the PAW Awards 2026 and the National Data Privacy Conference, was held at Okada, Manila on 27-28 May 2026. This year’s celebration also coincided with the NPC’s 10th anniversary, marking ten years since the establishment of the NPC as the country’s privacy watchdog. The PAW Awards 2026 carried the subtheme “10 for 10”, recognizing ten outstanding organizations and individuals for their contributions to privacy and data protection. The National Data Privacy Conference, with the subtheme “Digital Bayanihan: Nurturing Privacy Consciousness in the Age of AI,” focused on the opportunities and challenges brought by artificial intelligence and emerging technologies. In his keynote message, Secretary Henry R. Aguda of Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) emphasized the shared responsibility of protecting personal data in an increasingly digital society. “Privacy is no longer just a legal requirement. Cybersecurity is no longer just a technical concern. These are now shared national responsibilities. This is why we must ensure that we regulate AI while enabling innovation. We cannot slow down progress, but we must guide it,” Secretary Aguda stated. Looking Back: NPC Accomplishments in 2025 In his Privacy Commissioner’s Report, Atty. Johann Carlos S. Barcena highlighted the accomplishments and accolades received by the NPC in the past year across its five core mandates: public education, policy development, international cooperation, regulatory enforcement, and institutional governance. In the area of public education, the NPC expanded its reach beyond Metro Manila through nationwide roadshows conducted in Cebu, Davao, Pampanga, and Metro Manila, equipping 982 privacy practitioners with practical knowledge on responsible data processing and compliance. The NPC also convened the first-ever Government Sector Data Privacy Summit, gathering Data Protection Officers from local government units, national government agencies, government-owned and controlled corporations, and state universities and colleges. The NPC likewise continued to strengthen privacy awareness among the youth through its Kabataang Digital program. Since its launch in 2020, the initiative has engaged a cumulative total of 24,318 young Filipinos. Complementing these efforts were the NPC’s digital education initiatives, including “Rated DP with Josh,” which garnered more than 95,000 views and engagements, and “Privacy in the Spotlight,” which surpassed 640,000 total views and earned a Bronze recognition at the 2026 ASEAN Digital Awards in Vietnam. On policy development, the NPC issued several key issuances and advisories addressing emerging technologies and digital risks. Among these were the Guidelines on the Processing of Personal Data Collected Using Body-Worn Cameras, the clarification on Data Sharing Agreements, the Public Advisory on Online Lending Platforms issued jointly with the Department of Information and Communications Technology and the Securities and Exchange Commission, and the NPC’s first-ever Privacy Engineering Advisory, which institutionalized privacy-by-design principles across system lifecycle processes. The NPC also issued 16 advisory opinions and 215 complex inquiry responses involving lawful processing, data sharing, breaches, CCTV use, workplace disclosures, and data subject rights. On the international front, the NPC strengthened the Philippines’ position in global privacy governance. The agency hosted the 2025 Global Cross-Border Privacy Rules Forum Fall Workshop in Boracay Island, which gathered delegates from various countries. The NPC actively participated in more than 20 international bodies and working groups, including those under ASEAN, APEC, the Global Privacy Assembly, and the Asia Pacific Privacy Authorities Forum. Privacy Commissioner Barcena also highlighted the NPC’s strengthened enforcement and compliance efforts. Over the past year, the NPC handled 1,021 cases across multiple investigation streams. The NPC produced 2,159 enforcement outputs, including orders, technical reports, fact-finding reports, preliminary conferences, and adjudication referrals. It also conducted 2,390 compliance checks, 628 privacy sweeps, 54 on-site visits, and issued 1,377 citation tickets nationwide. These efforts led to increased compliance registrations, particularly in the healthcare sector, where approximately 2,100 healthcare professionals self-registered following NPC field visits. The NPC Registration System also expanded significantly, recording 17,140 registrations covering organizations, professionals, and exemptions across both public and private sectors. He further emphasized the NPC’s institutional recognitions, including the attainment of the following: PRIME-HRM Maturity Level II Bronze Award from the Civil Service Commission, five consecutive unmodified opinions from the Commission on Audit from 2021-2025 fiscal years, and Very Satisfactory ratings from the Department of Budget and Management’s Enhanced Agency Performance Review. Moving Forward: Building Trusted Growth in the Age of AI Looking ahead, Privacy Commissioner Barcena reaffirmed the NPC’s commitment to expanding privacy protection and strengthening public trust in an increasingly AI-driven digital environment. Privacy Commissioner Barcena emphasized the need for broader nationwide reach, noting that while registrations in the NPC Registration System have significantly increased, much of the growth remains concentrated in the National Capital Region. To address this, the NPC in partnership with the DICT, plans to establish regional privacy desks in Northern Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao to make the NPC more accessible to stakeholders across the country. Privacy Commissioner Barcena also underscored the importance of capacity building through the revival of the Data Privacy Competency Program, which aims to develop standardized training modules on privacy law and data protection for Data Protection Officers and the general public. The NPC is likewise strengthening its internal capabilities to address emerging concerns involving artificial intelligence, algorithmic systems, and digital governance. Privacy Commissioner Barcena further committed to ensuring that the NPC remains consistent, transparent, and timely in issuing guidance and decisions that will help both public and private sector stakeholders in navigating evolving privacy and technology issues. “The NPC’s role was to bring a regulator’s perspective into highly technical conversations: that privacy should not be treated as an afterthought, but as something designed into digital systems from the beginning,” he stated. Digital Bayanihan: Nurturing Privacy Consciousness in the Age of AI The conference gathered leaders and experts from government, industry, civil society, and the international privacy community for a series of panel discussions on AI governance, digital safety, and responsible innovation. Participating organizations and institutions included representatives from the Asia-Pacific privacy community, Future of Privacy Forum, Ayala Healthcare Holdings, Inc., Shopee, Analytics & Artificial Intelligence Association of the Philippines, Centre for Information Policy Leadership, Tech for Good Institute, TikTok, Mynt, Inc. (GCash), Meta, Roblox, Council for the Welfare of Children, Quisumbing Torres, the Department of Economy, Planning, and Development, UNESCO, and the NPC. 10 for 10: The PAW Awards 2026 The PAW Awards 2026, hosted by Deputy Privacy Commissioner Jose Sutton Belarmino II, recognized exemplary organizations and individuals who demonstrated excellence in privacy protection and data governance. Mynt, Inc. bagged four awards including Privacy Innovation Award, Privacy Initiative of the Year, Privacy Management Program of the Year. Its DPO, J.R. Robert Real, Jr., was also named as the Data Protection Officer of the Year. Converge ICT Solutions received the Kabataang Digital Award, while City Government of Muntinlupa was honored with the Public Sector Excellence Award. Credit Information Corporation received the Outstanding Technology Implementation for Data Protection Award. Atty. Kristine Tendencia-Bartolome of the Philippine Statistics Authority was recognized as the Privacy Advocate of the Year. The NPC Seal of Registration Compliance Excellence Award was conferred upon SM Retail, Inc. for private sector category and to the Philippine Statistics Authority for public sector category. As the NPC enters its second decade, the Privacy Commissioner Barcena reaffirmed the NPC’s commitment to building a privacy-conscious nation, strengthening public trust in digital systems, and ensuring that innovation and emerging technologies remain grounded in accountability, human rights, and responsible data governance. For more information, visit www.privacy.gov.ph . ### The post PAW 2026: NPC celebrates a decade of privacy leadership, calls for responsible AI governance appeared first on National Privacy Commission .

candidates.title: Japan and the Philippines strengthen data privacy protection cooperation
candidates.feed_text: TOKYO, JAPAN – The National Privacy Commission (NPC) of the Republic of the Philippines and the Personal Information Protection Commission (PPC) of Japan formally signed a Memorandum of Cooperation (MoC) to strengthen cross-border cooperation on personal data protection and privacy enforcement on 1 June 2026. The ceremonial signing was held at the PPC Office in Tokyo, Japan, and was signed by PPC Chairperson Dr. Satoru Tezuka and NPC Privacy Commissioner Atty. Johann Carlos S. Barcena, CESO III. The MoC acknowledges the growing need for international cooperation in safeguarding personal data amid the rapid and increasingly borderless flow of information in the digital age. Under the MoC, the NPC and the PPC will collaborate on information sharing and mutual assistance in privacy investigations, as well as exchange of best practices, and experiences on data protection policies and privacy-enhancing technologies. The MoC also opens opportunities for joint research initiatives, capacity-building activities, training and education programs, and other mutually agreed undertaking aimed at advancing data protection and privacy. Privacy Commissioner Barcena underscored the significance of the partnership in strengthening international privacy governance. “This agreement reflects our shared commitment to addressing the evolving challenges of privacy in the borderless digital environment. It likewise creates meaningful opportunities for the Philippines and Japan to exchange best practices and reinforce our collective efforts to uphold and advance personal data protection in an increasingly interconnected world,” he stated. Both authorities highlighted the vital role of international cooperation in addressing privacy risks arising from rapid technological developments and expanding global data flows. The MoC reaffirms the commitment of the Philippines and Japan to uphold the protection of personal information and deepen regulatory cooperation in support of a trusted and secure digital economy. ### The post Japan and the Philippines strengthen data privacy protection cooperation appeared first on National Privacy Commission .

candidates.title: Handhavingsbeleid AP gepubliceerd
candidates.feed_text: De Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens (AP) heeft het handhavingsbeleid openbaar gemaakt. Dit beleid gaat over de inzet van handhavingsinstrumenten als organisaties zich niet aan de privacyregels houden.

candidates.title: AP informeert incassobureaus over verantwoorde inzet AI
candidates.feed_text: Incassobureaus gebruiken steeds vaker algoritmes en AI, zo blijkt uit een steekproef van de Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens (AP) onder 29 bureaus. Het werk gaat hierdoor sneller, maar het leidt ook tot risico’s op onjuiste beslissingen, discriminatie en ongelijke behandeling. Om verkeerd gebruik van computersystemen te helpen voorkomen, komt de AP met aanbevelingen aan de incassosector.

candidates.title: AP onderzoekt websites vanwege misleidende cookiebanner
candidates.feed_text: De Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens (AP) is een onderzoek gestart naar 2 organisaties die een misleidende cookiebanner blijven gebruiken op hun website, ondanks uitleg en een waarschuwing van de AP. De cookiebanner van deze organisaties heeft geen direct zichtbare knop waarmee websitebezoekers volgsoftware (trackingcookies) kunnen weigeren. Hierdoor zullen bezoekers eerder trackingcookies accepteren.

candidates.title: Nieuwe EDPB-guidelines over samenspel DSA/AVG en AVG-boetes
candidates.feed_text: De European Data Protection Board (EDPB) heeft nieuwe guidelines vastgesteld voor de wisselwerking tussen de Algemene verordening gegevensbescherming (AVG) en de Digital Services Act (DSA). Daarnaast stelde de EDPB nieuwe guidelines op voor de procedure rond het opleggen van AVG-boetes.

candidates.title: AP zet volgende stap in toezicht op AI
candidates.feed_text: De Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens (AP) maakt zich verder klaar voor het toezicht op artificiële intelligentie (AI). Met de start van de nieuwe directie Toezicht en Coördinatie AI/Algoritmes (TCA) krijgt de taakopbouw steeds concreter vorm. De nieuwe directie gaat verder met het coördinerend toezicht op AI en algoritmes dat de AP sinds 2023 uitvoert. Daarnaast bereidt TCA het AI-markttoezicht voor en geeft TCA samen met de Rijksinspectie Digitale Infrastructuur (RDI) vorm aan de 'AI sandbox' en het gezamenlijke AI Coördinatiecentrum.

candidates.title: Wetsvoorstel kredietregistratie gaat goede kant op, maar nog aanpassingen nodig
candidates.feed_text: Op aandringen van de Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens (AP) werkt het kabinet aan privacy-vriendelijkere regels voor de kredietregistratie in Nederland. Die moeten zorgen voor een betere bescherming van persoonsgegevens bij het afsluiten van bijvoorbeeld een banklening of een telefoonabonnement. Een nieuw wetsvoorstel hierover gaat de goede kant op, maar moet volgens de AP op een aantal punten nog worden verbeterd.

candidates.title: AP waarschuwt gebruikers camerabrillen dat filmen van anderen vrijwel altijd verboden is
candidates.feed_text: Camerabrillen zijn bezig aan een snelle opmars. Wie daarmee andere mensen filmt of fotografeert, mag die beelden echter niet zomaar gebruiken, delen of publiceren. Ook mensen die toevallig in beeld komen en herkenbaar zijn, hebben recht op bescherming van hun privacy. Omdat veel gebruikers van camerabrillen dat niet weten, komt de Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens (AP) met uitleg van de privacyregels.

candidates.title: De samenleving wil lerende aanpak van de AP
candidates.feed_text: Op 14 september organiseerde de Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens (AP) het eerste Maatschappelijk Overleg met een brede vertegenwoordiging uit het maatschappelijke middenveld.

candidates.title: AP opent deuren tijdens Rondje Rechtsstaat: kom langs
candidates.feed_text: Bent u nieuwsgierig naar wat er zich afspeelt achter de deuren van de Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens (AP) aan het Lange Voorhout nummer 7 in Den Haag? En wat de AP voor u doet? Op zaterdag 12 september bent u van 10.00 tot 16.00 uur van harte welkom tijdens Rondje Rechtsstaat. We geven u graag een uniek inkijkje in de wereld van de AP.

candidates.title: Nieuw voor mkb: praktische sjablonen om aan de privacyregels te voldoen
candidates.feed_text: De Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens (AP) heeft 2 praktische documenten gepubliceerd speciaal voor het mkb. Het gaat om sjablonen voor een verwerkingsregister en een privacyverklaring. Ondernemers kunnen hiermee makkelijker voldoen aan de privacyregels en zo de persoonsgegevens van hun klanten beter beschermen. Ook helpen de sjablonen ondernemers om meer grip te krijgen op wat zij met persoonsgegevens doen en dit goed uit te leggen aan hun klanten.
